headline: Denied Demented FX's seasonal alcohol license at 530 Main Street; approved alcohol hours policy starting January 1, 2027.
summary: Three Special 1-Day Licenses, a 2026 open-air application, and a change of officers for Cracker Barrel were approved. Demented FX's one-day license was tabled until its work stop order is removed and building inspection approves its Certificate of Inspection. The owner of Appleton Market at 435 Appleton St. said police did not act on his complaints about loud music and people hanging around the store.
decisions: Denied the new seasonal all-alcohol on-premises license for Demented FX Inc. at 530 Main Street, 3-0, due to missing information and work permits.
Approved the Hours of Operation Alcohol Policy to take effect January 1, 2027, 3-0.
Approved the change of officers for Cracker Barrel Old Country Store Inc., 227 Whiting Farms Road, 3-0.
Approved the 2026 open-air application for Sweet Baby Rae's Sourdough, 3-0.
Approved the 2026 Special 1-Day License for White Lion Brewing, 3-0.
Approved the 2026 Special 1-Day License for Holyoke Community College, 3-0.
Tabled the 2026 Special 1-Day License for Demented FX, to be approved only after the work stop order is removed and building inspection approves the Certificate of Inspection, 3-0.
Approved the 2026 Special 1-Day License for Frances Santos, 3-0.
Approved sending letters asking licensees to attend the next meeting when a Police Report affecting them will be discussed, 3-0.

Old business 
• Closing Policy 
A motion was made by Anthony Luciano and seconded by Sam Mateo to approve the Hours of Operation Alcohol 
Policy to take effect January 1st, 2027. The Policy reads, “the hours of operation shall be restricted to those set by 
the Holyoke License Board and say on the base of the License. No patrons shall be on the premises before the official 
opening hours or after the official closing hour of 2 a.m. No entry after 1:10 a.m. and patrons who leave the 
establishment after 1:10 a.m. may not re-enter the establishment. The lights must be on, and the music must stop at 
1:45 a.m. Last call for an alcohol sale shall be completed by 1:30 a.m. and no alcohol may be served after 1:45 a.m.  
Last call should be announced no later than 1:30 a.m. All patrons must move off the premises by 2 a.m. Licensees 
with managers employing contractors shall not be prohibited from being upon the premises at any time for the 
purpose of cleaning, making renovations, making emergency repairs to provide security for such premises for 
preparing food for the day's business, for opening or closing the business. MGL Chapter 39 Section 12.” The motion 
carried 3-0. 
 
New Business:  
• Appleton Market Complaint-435 Appleton St. 
Anthony Luciano read out the Police report to the Appleton Market representatives present at the Meeting. 
The Appleton Market owner said he had complained to the Police about loud music, and people hanging around the 
store, but the Police do nothing. 
Alex Maysonet said there is no other issue with the establishment. I drive there a lot of times. I go visit your store 
for lunchtime. You are only here because of the complaint. 
Jose Correa said he thinks we need to fix the issue with the Police Department and the Councilor. We know we 
never had an issue with your establishment. Thank you for coming to our Meeting today. Continue to call the police. 
 Alex Maysonet added the biggest problem is you hold the Liquor License and, according to the email, they’re 
purchasing the alcohol and then drinking it outside. By law, that is a violation of your License. So, I get the 
confrontation, because I don't like confrontation either. But you do have to protect your License because if we keep 
getting complaints about people drinking eventually, you're going to get a violation and that goes on your License. 
Even the parking lot has a License permit.

• Minutes-  
No Minutes to approve. 
 
• Matters not reasonably anticipated by the Chair. 
Anthony Luciano said the Police are proactive about having a system in place when they have an incident. 
They're going to assign a liaison to them specifically for the License Board, and they're going to have a process in 
place so that whenever there's an issue with a Licensed business, they will get a report filled out and sent over to us 
right away. So, the Mayor’s going to put that in place. Right now, when we get a Police Report, Alex presents the 
Police Report, we decide and usually vote “yes” to bring them in. And I'm wondering if we could just speed that up 
to where Alex gets a Police Report-she immediately reaches out to the Licensee and tells them, “A Police Report will 
be happening at this Meeting, you’re requested to attend,” and I want to get the License Board’s vote on that. 
 
A motion was made by Anthony Luciano and seconded by Jose Correa whereby any Police Reports affecting 
Licensees, Alex will contact them by letter, requesting their attendance at the next License Board Meeting where the 
Police Report will be discussed. The motion carried 3-0.
